1.meaning: All praise, commendation, and grateful acknowledgement — the recognition that beauty, goodness, and perfection rightly belong to and are owed to the one being praised. As a definite noun with the article 'al-', it conveys that the totality of praise is encompassed.
1.grammar: A definite noun (carrying the article 'al-', 'the'). The final '-u' ending is nominative: it marks the word as the subject or main topic of a statement — the thing being talked about or the doer of an action, rather than its object.
1.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise, to commend, to give thanks

2.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
2.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

3.meaning: 'Originator', 'Bringer-into-being', 'Maker who splits forth creation from nothing'. The word names the one who first brings things into existence, cleaving them into being where there was none.

parts.en: originator / one who brings into being

3.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun: 'the one who originates'). The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically links the word to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. As a doer-noun it can also take an object after it.
3.root: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to split, cleave, bring forth, originate

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
5.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

7.meaning: 'The angels' — the plural of 'angel': the noble created beings who serve and obey Allah and carry out His commands.
7.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the.' Malāʾika is the broken (irregular) plural of malak, 'angel.' The final tā' marbūṭa (ة) is part of this collective/group plural's standard form — it is not a 'plural' marker by itself. The case vowel on it is the genitive -i (heard as -ti), the ending used after a preposition or to link 'of,' signalling the noun is the object of a preceding preposition.
7.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — the root underlying malak, 'angel' (a messenger/emissary)

8.meaning: 'messengers' — envoys, those sent by Allah bearing a message to people.
8.grammar: The broken (irregular) plural of rasūl ('messenger'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, typically marking the word as a direct object and indefinite ('messengers').

9.meaning: Possessors of / those endowed with. A word meaning 'owners of' or 'people having' some quality, used to attribute a trait or rank to a group.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'possessors/people of', which has no singular from its own letters (its singular is supplied by another word). The 'ī' ending here reflects its non-nominative (genitive/accusative) form and it is always followed by a noun naming what is possessed ('possessors OF …').

12.meaning: In threes — three at a time, or three each. A distributive numeral meaning 'three by three'.
12.grammar: A distributive numeral from the root for 'three', meaning 'three apiece'. It is diptote — its ending here is -a rather than the usual -in, because this pattern does not take the indefinite -n and uses -a in place of -i. The wa- prefix means 'and' or 'or'.
12.root: ث-ل-ث (th-l-th) — three, a third

13.meaning: In fours — four at a time, or four each. A distributive numeral meaning 'four by four'.
13.grammar: A distributive numeral from the root for 'four', meaning 'four apiece'. Like its companions it is diptote, so its ending is -a rather than the usual indefinite -in. The wa- prefix means 'and' or 'or'.
13.root: ر-ب-ع (r-b-ʿ) — four, a fourth

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'he/it increases, adds, grows greater.' It conveys augmentation — something becoming more, or one thing adding more to another.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular doer ('he/it'). The final -u is the indicative ending, which marks a plain, factual statement of an ongoing or habitual action ('it increases').
14.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, grow, add, exceed

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: "the creation; the make/build (of a thing); physical form or constitution" — that which is created, or the manner in which something is fashioned.
16.grammar: A definite noun ("the" via al-). The -i ending is the genitive case, typically used after a preposition or to link it to a following noun ("… OF …").

17.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
17.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

18.meaning: "He wills / wishes / desires" — denotes an act of will or volition, the choosing of something. As an ongoing/present-tense verb it expresses willing as a continuous, sovereign act.
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he wills').

19.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
19.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
20.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

21.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
21.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

22.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
22.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

23.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
23.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
23.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

24.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
24.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
4.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
7.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

9.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
9.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

14.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
14.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
17.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

18.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
18.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

19.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
19.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
19.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
2.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
2.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

3.meaning: 'Remember! / call to mind, mention' — a command to bring something to mind, keep it in memory, or speak of it.
3.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The '-ū' ending directs the order to a group ('you all remember!'); the initial connecting 'a-' is a helping vowel that lets the word begin.

4.meaning: A favor, blessing, or grace bestowed; the bounty and kindness shown by a giver, especially the abundant gifts of Allah.
4.grammar: A feminine singular noun ('favor'). The final tā' is pronounced (rather than as silent -h) because the word is in a construct chain, joining to a following noun ('the favor of …'); the -a ending here marks the accusative case, typical of a direct object.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
6.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

7.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
7.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: 'Other than, except, not' — a word of exception or difference that sets one thing apart from another, or negates an attribute ('non-…').
10.grammar: A noun of exclusion meaning 'other than.' It governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than ___ '). The '-u' nominative ending typically reflects its agreement with, or role describing, a preceding nominative noun.

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: 'He provides for you / grants you sustenance' — to bestow provision, livelihood, and the means of life. With the attached 'you', it speaks of the One supplying a group with what they need to live.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), shown by the 'ya-' prefix. The base ends in '-u' (indicative, a plain ongoing statement). The attached '-kum' is the object 'you' (a group): 'he provides for you'.
12.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide; provision, sustenance, livelihood

13.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
13.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

14.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
14.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

15.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
15.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

16.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
16.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

17.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
17.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
17.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

18.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
18.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

20.meaning: An interrogative of manner or place meaning 'how?', 'in what way?', or 'whence / from where?'. It expresses wonder or challenge at how something could be so, often implying 'how on earth…?'.
20.grammar: A connective 'fa' ('so/then') joined to an indeclinable question-word. Being a fixed particle, it has no case ending; it opens a question about manner or source and carries a tone of astonishment or rebuke.

21.meaning: To be turned away, diverted, or deluded — driven from truth to falsehood, made to deviate from what is right. The passive sense is 'to be deflected / led astray' from a correct course.
21.grammar: A present/future-tense passive verb, second-person masculine plural: 'you (all) are turned away'. The vowel pattern (u-a) marks it passive — the subject has the action done to it — and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject in the ongoing (indicative) mood.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

3.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
3.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'she/it was called a liar, was denied, was rejected as false.' It is the passive of the intensive 'to charge with lying' — the action is undergone rather than performed.

parts.en: to be charged with lying / be rejected as false (passive)

4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice and intensive pattern; the middle letter carries a doubling shadda and the internal vowels (u–i) mark it as passive, so the subject receives the action. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject ('she/it was …'), viewed as a completed action.
4.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this pattern, to be called a liar / denied

5.meaning: Messengers — the plural of 'messenger': those sent with a commission to convey a message; in religious usage, prophets sent with revelation.
5.grammar: A plural noun. The final '-un' (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative: it marks 'messengers' (no 'the') and signals that the word is functioning as a subject or naming a thing rather than being possessed or governed by a preposition.
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, dispatch a message

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
7.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
7.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

8.meaning: And to / and toward; a connector "and" joined with a preposition expressing direction or destination toward which something moves or is referred.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning "to/toward," prefixed with the connector wa- ("and"). Being a preposition, it puts the noun that follows it into the genitive case (the "…toward X" relationship). It has no case ending of its own.

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: It is returned / brought back; a present-tense passive action of being sent or referred back to a source or destination.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing verb in the passive voice, so the action is done to the subject ("is returned/brought back"). The tu- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular (or non-human plural) subject ("it/they"). The final -u ending signals the indicative mood, used for stating an action.

1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

4.meaning: 'a promise / pledge' — a binding assurance of something to come; here as a noun naming the thing pledged or the act of pledging.
4.grammar: A verbal noun with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as a direct object or as an emphatic inner object reinforcing a verb of the same meaning ('a promise [truly promised]'). It names the act/content of promising.
4.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give an assurance

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'Truth, reality, a rightful due' — that which is firmly real, correct, and established; also a right or claim that is owed. As a descriptor it means 'true, real, well-founded.'
6.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -un ending (nominative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) is the form a noun takes as the subject or as the completing word of a statement ('is true/real').
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, what is due

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
7.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

9.meaning: 'The life' — earthly existence, the span of living in this world. The word denotes life as the state of being alive, vitality, and the worldly life as a whole.
9.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the'. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something), or as the predicate naming what something is.

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

13.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
13.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
13.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The Shayṭān / the Satan — the rebellious, evil one who tempts and misleads; broadly any defiant, alienating force that incites toward wrong.
2.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', 'the'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative case, which most often signals the word is the direct object of a verb. (The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'sh' in pronunciation.)
2.root: Disputed in classical lexicography. Many derive it from ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — being far/remote and rebellious (hence one distant from good and given to defiance), treating the final nūn as radical. Others derive it from ش-ي-ط (sh-y-ṭ), from شَاطَ 'to burn, blaze, perish', treating the nūn as an added letter. Both are attested (e.g., in Lisān al-ʿArab).

3.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'enemy', 'foe', or 'adversary' — one who shows hostility or opposition. The single Arabic form can refer to one enemy or collectively to enemies.
4.grammar: A noun carrying the -un ending: nominative case (typically the subject, or the completing word after 'to be') combined with tanwīn, the indefinite '-n' that marks it as 'an enemy' rather than 'the enemy'.
4.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — hostility, enmity, transgressing a limit

6.meaning: 'An enemy / a foe' — one who is hostile or opposed; can refer to a single enemy or collectively to enemies.
6.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'enemy', on a pattern with a doubled final consonant. The -an ending (tanwīn) is accusative plus indefiniteness, the form used for the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain verbs (e.g. 'took/became an enemy').

7.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
7.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

8.meaning: 'He/it calls, summons, invites, calls upon, prays to' — a verb for calling out to someone, inviting them, or supplicating.
8.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb from a weak-final root, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks the masculine singular subject; the stem ends in a long ū from the weak final letter.

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: Companions, associates, fellows; those who keep company with or belong to a thing — people closely bound to something (often 'people/inhabitants of …').
12.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of ṣāḥib ('companion'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a following noun ('companions OF …') or follows a preposition. As a plural it denotes a group, here in a possessive/linking relationship.
12.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, to accompany, keep company

13.meaning: The Blaze — a fiercely kindled, flaming fire. On its pattern the word stresses an intensely blazing, raging fire, and it is used as a name for the punishing Fire.
13.grammar: The al- prefix is the definite article 'the'; its 'l' assimilates into the following 's' in pronunciation (heard as-saʿīr). The word is on the faʿīl pattern, here conveying an intense, kindled fire. The final -i is the genitive ending, used after a preposition or in possessive linkage ('… OF …').
13.root: س-ع-ر (s-ʿ-r) — to kindle, blaze, flare up

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
2.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

3.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

4.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
4.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

6.meaning: A connective phrase: 'and those who…' — the joining word 'and' attached to a masculine-plural relative pronoun that points to a group of people about whom something is then stated.
6.grammar: A particle of joining (wa, 'and') prefixed to a relative pronoun. 'Alladhīna' is masculine plural and indeclinable (its form does not change for case); it means 'those who / the ones who' and introduces a clause describing the group. The doubled 'w' reflects assimilation in pronunciation to a preceding word.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
7.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
7.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

8.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
8.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

9.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
9.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
9.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

10.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

11.meaning: Forgiveness — Allah's covering over and pardoning of sins; the act and gift of having one's faults effaced.
11.grammar: A verbal noun of the 'mafʿila' pattern, naming the abstract action of forgiving. The '-tun' ending combines the feminine '-t-' with '-un', the nominative-indefinite marker, which typically marks an indefinite subject ('a forgiveness') — the one acting or being asserted to exist.

12.meaning: 'And a reward / recompense / wage' — payment or recompense earned for one's work or deeds, joined by 'and'.
12.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a reward') preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The -un ending is indefinite ('a/an') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for something being introduced/named.
12.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense

1.meaning: An interrogative formed from three pieces meaning roughly 'Is then the one who…?' It opens a rhetorical question that compares two parties. The 'a-' is a question marker, 'fa-' links to a preceding statement and means 'then/so', and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'the one who / whoever'.
1.grammar: A combination of particles plus the relative pronoun 'man'. The leading 'a-' turns the sentence into a yes/no question (often rhetorical). 'fa-' is a connective meaning 'then/so', tying the question to what came before. 'man' refers to a person and introduces a clause describing them ('the one who…'); it does not change its ending for case.

2.meaning: It was made beautiful / adorned / made alluring; the act of decorating something or making it appear attractive and appealing.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice on an intensive (form II) pattern, so the action is done to the subject and stresses thorough adorning ("was made beautiful/alluring"). The -u-…-i- vowel pattern marks the passive, and the final -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("it/he").

3.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
3.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

7.meaning: Good, fine, beautiful, excellent — pleasing and praiseworthy in quality. It describes something done well or possessing goodness and beauty.
7.grammar: An adjective ('good'). The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite). As an adjective it agrees with and describes a noun; the accusative case matches a noun in that same case.
7.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

8.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
8.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'he leads astray' or 'he lets go astray' — to cause someone to lose the right way, to misguide or allow to wander from the correct path.
10.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the causative (form IV) pattern. The yu- prefix marks third-person singular with the vowel typical of derived causative verbs, and the final -u marks the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The causative pattern gives the sense of 'causing to go astray'.
10.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, err

11.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
11.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

12.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
12.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
12.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

13.meaning: 'And he/it guides, leads rightly, directs to the way' — a verb for showing the right path and leading someone toward correct guidance.
13.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb from a weak-final root, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks the masculine singular subject and the stem ends in a long ī; the prefixed wa- means 'and'.
13.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, leading to the right way

14.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
14.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

16.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
16.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

19.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
19.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
19.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

20.meaning: Regrets, sorrows, or anguished grief — deep pangs of remorse and distress over loss or missed opportunity, so intense they consume the heart.
20.grammar: An indefinite feminine sound plural ('regrets, sorrows'; plural of ḥasra). The -āt is the feminine plural marker; the final -in (tanwīn) is the ending used for such plurals in the genitive or accusative, here also signalling indefiniteness ('regrets').
20.root: ح-س-ر (ḥ-s-r) — to grieve, regret; to be exhausted/laid bare

21.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
21.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

23.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
23.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

24.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
24.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

25.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'they make / do / fashion / produce.' The root implies skilled, deliberate crafting — to work something with care and bring it about by one's own effort.
25.grammar: A present/future verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' as the doers. The closing -na shows the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action that is simply being stated. The root carries a sense of purposeful workmanship.
25.root: ص-ن-ع (ṣ-n-ʿ) — to make, craft, fashion with skill

1.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
1.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: To send, dispatch, or send forth — to commission someone or something and set it on its way toward a destination or purpose.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb (causative Form IV) for a third-person masculine singular subject: 'he sent' or 'he dispatched.' The a- prefix and the pattern give the causative sense (to cause to go / send off); the final -a is the standard 'he (did it)' past-tense ending.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, commissioning a messenger

4.meaning: The winds — moving currents of air. A plural noun denoting winds, often associated with bringing rain and mercy.
4.grammar: A definite plural noun. The -a ending is accusative, which generally marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon). The "l" of "al-" assimilates into the following "r" (al-riyāḥ → ar-riyāḥ).
4.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — wind, breath, spirit; rest, relief

6.meaning: Cloud, or a mass/collection of clouds; the gathered vapor that carries rain. A collective noun for cloud-matter.
6.grammar: An indefinite collective noun in the accusative case. The -an (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ("a cloud / clouds") and accusative, a case that generally marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
6.root: س-ح-ب (s-ḥ-b) — to drag, draw along; cloud (drawn across the sky)

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
8.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'a land', 'a town', or 'a region' — a settled place or territory, often one inhabited by people.
9.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a land') and in the genitive case, which typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

10.meaning: Dead, lifeless; devoid of life. As a description of land it means barren and unproductive, as if dead.
10.grammar: An indefinite adjective in the genitive case. The -in (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive; an adjective in this case typically agrees with and describes a preceding genitive noun (such as one following a preposition).

12.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
12.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.
12.root: — (preposition with pronoun; no root)

13.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
13.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'
13.root: أ-ر-ض (ʼ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

14.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
14.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
14.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

15.meaning: Its death, its lifelessness or dormancy; the state of being dead, joined to a possessor.
15.grammar: A noun ('death') with an attached third-person feminine singular possessive pronoun ('its / her'). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, the case taken before a possessor pronoun and after prepositions ('death of it').

16.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
16.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
16.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

17.meaning: the rising / the resurrection — the act of being raised up and dispersed abroad; the bringing back of the dead to life and their spreading forth.

parts.en: rising, being raised and scattered abroad

17.grammar: A verbal noun made definite by al- ('the'); the l of al- assimilates into the following n (a 'sun letter'), giving the doubled n in the transliteration ('an-nushūr'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject or predicate ('the resurrection [is] …'). It names the event of the dead being raised and dispersed.
17.root: ن-ش-ر (n-sh-r) — to spread out, unfold, revive; to raise and scatter abroad (the resurrection)

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
3.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
3.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

4.meaning: Might, honour, and unassailable strength; the quality of being mighty and held in high esteem, beyond reach of humiliation.
4.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the might/honour'). The -ta ending (the t of the feminine ending plus an -a) is accusative, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
4.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dearness, being unassailable

5.meaning: Then belonging to Allah; so it is Allah's. The phrase asserts that something pertains or belongs exclusively to Allah, introduced by a connective 'then/so'.
5.grammar: A connective 'fa-' ('then/so') plus the preposition 'li-' ('to/for/belonging to') attached to the name Allah. The '-i' ending on the name is genitive, the case required after a preposition; the combination expresses ownership or entitlement: '(it is) for/belonging to Allah'.

6.meaning: Might, honor, dignity, and the sense of being above others — a mix of rightful strength/glory and, in a person, self-exalting pride and disdain that resists correction.
6.grammar: A definite feminine noun (with 'al-' = 'the'); the 'ة' (tā' marbūṭa) is the feminine ending. The final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the noun as the subject/doer of a sentence or the thing being described ('… the pride seized him').
6.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, honor, being mighty/inaccessible

7.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
7.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.
7.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — gathering, joining, bringing together

8.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

11.meaning: The good, wholesome, pure one; that which is sweet, clean, fertile, and pleasing. "Ṭayyib" combines the senses of goodness, purity, and agreeableness — of land, it means rich and fertile.
11.grammar: A definite adjective in the nominative case. The final -u marks the nominative; an adjective in this case typically agrees with and describes a preceding nominative noun (such as a subject). The "l" of "al-" assimilates into the following "ṭ" (al-ṭayyib → aṭ-ṭayyib).
11.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — to be good, pure, wholesome, pleasant

15.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

16.meaning: 'They scheme / they plot.' A present-tense verb from 'makara', to devise a hidden stratagem or plan. Describes an ongoing or habitual plotting by a group.
16.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks the third person; the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood (the default mood for a plain statement). It conveys ongoing or repeated action: 'they keep plotting'.
16.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to scheme, plot, devise a cunning plan

17.meaning: 'The evil deeds / bad actions' — plural of sayyi'a, a wrong or evil act, a misdeed or sin; the opposite of a good deed.
17.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the misdeeds'). The -i ending here is the case marker for the sound feminine plural in the genitive/accusative state, typically signalling that it follows a preposition, links to a preceding noun, or stands as an object.
17.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; misdeed, wrong

18.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
18.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

19.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
19.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

20.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty in force. Describes something powerful and unrelenting in its strength or rigor.
20.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting a firmly established quality (intensity, severity). The final -un ending combines the nominative case (used for the subject or a predicate describing who/what something is) with nunation (the -n sound), which marks the word as indefinite, i.e. 'a severe one' rather than 'the severe one'.
20.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

22.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
22.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

23.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
23.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

1.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
1.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

2.meaning: 'He created you' — He brought you into existence, originating and shaping you. The verb denotes bringing something into being and giving it its form and proportion, here with 'you (plural)' as the one(s) created.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer in the completed past ('he created'). The suffix '-kum' is the object 'you (plural),' i.e. the ones to whom the action was done.

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: 'Dust / earth / soil.' The noun turāb denotes dust or dry earth — the fine soil of the ground.
4.grammar: A masculine noun. The -in ending marks it as indefinite ('dust / some dust') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition (e.g., 'from …') or when linked to a preceding noun.

5.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
5.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: A drop of fluid; a tiny quantity of sperm/seminal fluid — by extension the minute beginning from which a human is formed.
7.grammar: A feminine noun (the '-a(t)' is its feminine form). The final '-in' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …') and in the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
7.root: ن-ط-ف (n-ṭ-f) — to drip, trickle; a drop of fluid

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: He made you, He appointed/rendered you (plural) — to bring into a state or set in a role. The verb can mean 'to make/create' or 'to designate as', with the attached object 'you (all)'.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he …'); the bare stem with the open ending marks completed action. The attached -kum is the second-person masculine plural object pronoun 'you all'. So: 'He made/appointed you (all)'.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'spouses', 'mates', or 'wives' — the plural of a word denoting one of a pair joined together, hence a husband or wife. Context determines whether husbands or wives are meant.
10.grammar: A plural noun with the -an ending, which is accusative and indefinite. The accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The azC-ā-C shape is a broken-plural pattern. The singular denotes either partner of a married pair.
10.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, to join as a couple; spouse, mate

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: 'she/it carries / bears / is pregnant with' — to hold, bear, or carry a load, including bearing a child.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix here marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'). The -u ending marks the indicative mood, the verb's normal affirmative form ('she carries').
12.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear, be pregnant

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
13.root: — (preposition)

14.meaning: A female — a female being, whether human or animal; the counterpart of 'male'.
14.grammar: A singular noun denoting a female. It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case, so its grammatical role is shown by context rather than by a final vowel.

15.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

17.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
17.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

19.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
19.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

20.meaning: 'He is given a long life / he is granted length of years' — to have one's lifespan extended, to be made to live long.
20.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The yu- prefix with the -u vowel pattern marks third-person masculine singular passive ('he is/can be …-ed'). The doubled middle consonant belongs to the intensive (Form II) pattern, here carrying the sense 'to be granted a long/extended life'. The final -u is the indicative ending, used for a plain ongoing or general action.

21.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
21.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

23.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
23.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

25.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
25.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

27.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
27.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

28.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
28.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

29.meaning: A Book, a scripture — a written record or revealed text. In sacred usage it denotes a divinely revealed Scripture. The indefinite form means 'a book / some scripture' rather than a specific one.
29.grammar: A noun. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending: it marks the word as indefinite ('a book') and in the genitive case, the case typically used after a preposition or when one noun is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
29.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; 'kitāb' = something written, a book

30.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
30.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

31.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
31.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

32.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
32.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
32.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

33.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
33.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'They are equal / it is the same' — to be on a par, level, or alike; to stand even with one another with no difference of value.
2.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is equal'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a present action; the weak final letter (from the root's last 'w/y') appears as the long ending. It expresses things being on the same level.

4.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
4.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and this (one)' — the pointing word 'this' (for something near, masculine/neutral) joined to 'and'.
9.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to the demonstrative hādhā ('this'), used to point to something near at hand (masculine singular). A demonstrative like this has a fixed ending and does not change for grammatical case; it can stand as a subject or be linked to a following noun ('this ___').

12.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
12.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

13.meaning: 'Of every / each' — kull denotes the totality or entirety of a class; with this indefinite ending it means 'every (one)' or 'all'.
13.grammar: A noun bearing the ending -in, which combines the genitive case (used after a preposition or to link 'of …') with nunation — the final -n marking the word as indefinite ('every/any').
13.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, the whole, allness.

14.meaning: You eat — to consume food; addressed to a group, describing an ongoing or habitual action.
14.grammar: The ta- prefix plus the -ūna ending mark the subject as 'you (masculine plural)'. The full -ūna ending (with its final nūn intact) is the indicative mood, presenting the eating as a real, ongoing or habitual fact rather than something negated or made conditional.

15.meaning: 'Flesh' or 'meat' — the soft muscular tissue of the body.
15.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (accusative with the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness) typically marks it as a direct object or as the substance with which something is covered or supplied, and signals 'some / a' rather than 'the'.

16.meaning: Fresh, tender, and moist — newly formed and soft, as fresh meat or just-ripened produce. It describes something in a supple, just-obtained state.
16.grammar: An adjective, masculine singular. The final -an (accusative with tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and typically as an object or descriptive complement ('… as fresh').
16.root: ط-ر-و / ط-ر-ي (ṭ-r-w/y) — to be fresh, tender, moist
