18.meaning: Ornament, jewelry, or adornment — decorative finery such as is worn to beautify, often crafted from precious materials.
18.grammar: A feminine singular noun; the feminine tā' marbūṭa is part of the stem. The final diacritic -an (accusative tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and typically as a direct object ('… an ornament').

19.meaning: 'You wear it / them' — the act of putting on and clothing oneself with something, with the attached pronoun pointing to the feminine thing being worn.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb of wearing with an attached object pronoun. The ta- prefix and -ūna ending mean 'you (plural) do/are doing'; the retained nūn marks ongoing present/future action; the attached -hā means 'it/them', referring to a feminine thing.
19.root: ل-ب-س (l-b-s) — to wear, put on clothing

20.meaning: "and you see / would see" — to perceive with the eyes or to behold; also "to regard" something as being a certain way.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb in the second-person masculine singular: the ta- prefix means "you (one man)." This verb comes from a weak root, so its final weak letter shows as the long -ā vowel; in the indicative it expresses ongoing or potential seeing.

21.meaning: The ship, ark, or vessel — a boat that travels on water. The noun is unusual in that the same form serves for both singular ('a ship') and plural ('ships').
21.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks a noun as the direct object of a verb or the subject after certain particles.
21.root: ف-ل-ك (f-l-k) — that which is round or revolves; hence both a sailing ship and the orbiting celestial sphere.

22.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
22.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

23.meaning: Cleaving or ploughing through — describing ships that cut through the water, parting the waves as they sail. The plural of an active participle portraying that surging, furrowing motion.
23.grammar: A plural active participle (those that cleave the water), of the special 'diptote' pattern. The final -a here serves as the accusative (object/descriptive complement); nouns of this pattern take no tanwīn.
23.root: م-خ-ر (m-kh-r) — to cleave/plough through water (of a ship)

24.meaning: 'So that you may seek / strive after / pursue.' Expresses purpose — seeking out something desired, such as bounty or gain.
24.grammar: The front li- means 'so that / in order to' and puts the verb into the subjunctive (a mood for purpose and intention). The ta- prefix plus the -ū ending together mark the doer as 'you all' (a group); the subjunctive is why the ending is -ū rather than -ūna. The verb is a form VIII pattern meaning 'to seek out, pursue.'

25.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
25.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

26.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
26.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
26.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

27.meaning: And so that you (plural) may; in the hope that you might. The particle laʿalla expresses hope, expectation, or a desired outcome ('perhaps / so that'), here with 'you' as its subject.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in the hope that

27.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps / in hope that'), which expresses an anticipated or hoped-for result, with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all') as its subject. Such particles place the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -kum here is that subject. It typically leads into a verb stating the hoped outcome. The wa- ('and') links it to what comes before.

28.meaning: 'You (all) give thanks / are grateful'. To recognize a kindness and acknowledge it — with the heart, tongue, and deeds — toward the one who bestowed it.
28.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix signals a 'you' subject, and the '-ūna' ending marks a plural masculine 'you' in the ongoing (indicative) mood — 'you all give thanks'. The retained '-na' shows the verb stands free of any negating or governing particle.

2.meaning: The night — al-layl is the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; the dark portion of the day-night cycle, a time of covering, rest and stillness.
2.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically given to the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or used adverbially for time ('the night').

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.
4.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the,' with its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the day') or as following a preposition or a particle that governs the genitive.

6.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.
6.grammar: A definite singular noun ('al-' = 'the,' its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n'). The final '-a' is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise signals 'as / being' something.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
8.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

9.meaning: And He made (something) subservient, harnessed it, or pressed it into service — to bring a thing under control so it works toward an appointed purpose.
9.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The verb is past tense for 'he' (third-person masculine singular); its doubled middle letter marks an intensive/causative pattern ('to make subservient'), and the -a ending is the standard past-tense vowel for a single masculine doer who completed the act.
9.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to subject, subdue, press into service

10.meaning: The sun — the blazing daytime luminary.
10.grammar: A feminine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'all,' 'each,' 'every,' or 'the whole.' It denotes totality — that the entirety of a group or thing is included.
12.grammar: A noun in the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (the -un ending), which marks it as indefinite and as the subject or doer of a sentence. Standing alone with tanwīn it carries the sense 'everyone / all of them' as an independent subject.
12.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

13.meaning: It flows, runs, or courses along — used of water, rivers, ships, or anything moving smoothly and continuously.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final long -ī belongs to the weak-rooted stem and signals the ongoing, habitual action of flowing.
13.root: ج-ر-ي (j-r-y) — to flow, run, course, stream

14.meaning: 'For a term / for an appointed time' — the preposition 'for' joined to 'a fixed period or appointed deadline,' the stretch of time set for something.
14.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('for/to'). The final -in is the indefinite genitive ('a …'): the tanwīn (-n) marks indefiniteness, and the -i is the genitive case, required here because the word follows a preposition.
14.root: ء-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — fixed term, appointed time, deadline

15.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'named, specified, designated, made definite.' It describes something that has been clearly stated and fixed by name — a term that is precisely set rather than vague.
15.grammar: A passive participle (the mu- prefix forms a 'one that is …' word from the Form II intensive pattern, with a doubled middle root letter) meaning 'named/specified.' It carries the indefinite ending -an, written with alif maqṣūra (a final ya-shaped letter sounded as -ā). Because it ends in this weak final letter, the form stays the same whether nominative, accusative, or genitive — context shows it is describing an indefinite noun.
15.root: س-م-ي (s-m-y) — name, naming; to give or assign a name

16.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' — a pointing word that singles out something distant or already mentioned, addressed to a group of people ('that, O you [plural]').
16.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', built from the base 'dhā' plus the distance-marker 'l-' and the plural-addressee particle '-kum' ('you all'). The final 'u' on '-kumu' is a connecting vowel used when the next word begins with a definite article. It does not change for case.

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
17.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

18.meaning: Your (plural) Lord — 'Rabb' means the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion. It combines lordship with loving upbringing and care.
18.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix '-kum' means 'your' (plural possessor). The '-u' on 'rabbu' before the suffix is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or as a predicate standing on its own.
18.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, own

19.meaning: To him / for him / he has — the preposition 'to/for' fused with a pronoun meaning 'him.' It expresses belonging, benefit, or possession (something is 'his' or done 'for him').
19.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with the attached 3rd-person masculine singular pronoun 'him.' The pairing means 'to him' or 'for him' and often conveys possession ('he has …') or that an action is directed toward his benefit or detriment.
19.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

20.meaning: 'The kingship / sovereignty / dominion' — al-mulk is rule and royal authority itself, the power and right to govern.
20.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence (the thing that 'is' or does something).

21.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
21.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

22.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
22.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

23.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
23.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

24.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

24.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

25.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
25.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

26.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they own, possess, or have power/control over'; it conveys having mastery and the authority to dispose of something — to hold it in one's power, whether benefit or harm.
26.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The -ūna ending marks 'they (masculine plural)' in the indicative mood, the plain-statement form; it shortens to -ū when a governing particle precedes.
26.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, have dominion

27.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
27.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: 'You call them / you invoke them' — a present-tense verb. From the root for calling, it covers summoning, appealing to, or invoking someone (as in calling upon a deity). The attached pronoun is the object, 'them.'
2.grammar: A present-tense action with a 'you' (masculine) subject built into the ta- prefix. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural). The verb commonly carries the sense of calling upon or invoking.
2.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray to

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: 'They hear / they listen.' A verb of perceiving sound; by extension, to heed or pay attention to what is said.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb for a plural 'they' (masculine): the ya- prefix with the -ū ending marks the masculine plural subject. The missing final nūn indicates a subjunctive/jussive mood, typical after a negating or conditioning particle.

6.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
6.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they heard / they listened' — to perceive by ear, and by extension to give ear and pay heed.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The silent alif written after the wāw (-ū) is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
7.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening, heeding

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'they answered / responded / complied'. The core sense is giving a favourable response to a call or request — to hearken and obey when summoned.
9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action; it is built on a derived (augmented) pattern and on a hollow (weak-middle) root, so the middle root-letter surfaces as the long vowel -ā- of the stem rather than as a consonant. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did…'). (The final silent alif is just a spelling convention after this plural -ū.)
9.root: ج-و-ب (j-w-b) — to answer, respond, reply (hollow/weak-middle root)

10.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

11.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
11.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

12.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
12.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
12.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

13.meaning: 'They disbelieve / reject faith', or more literally 'they cover over (the truth), they are ungrateful'. An ongoing or habitual rejection and denial.
13.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually; the final -na (kept, not dropped) shows the verb is in its plain indicative form, stating an ongoing fact.
13.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering over; hence disbelief and ingratitude

15.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

17.meaning: 'The like (of),' 'an equivalent,' 'something matching or comparable.' It denotes a counterpart of equal measure or kind to something else.
17.grammar: A noun in the nominative case, shown by the final -u, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('X is …'). It is regularly followed by a noun in the genitive to mean 'the like OF …'.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
2.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
2.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

3.meaning: You (a group of males) — the detached/standalone pronoun for a plural 'you', used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own. The final short vowel is a connecting vowel before a following word.
3.grammar: Independent (standalone) personal pronoun, second-person masculine plural, 'you all'. It does not attach to another word; it stands alone to emphasize or identify the subject. The final '-u' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word.

5.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
5.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
7.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
7.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

8.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
8.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

9.meaning: The Self-Sufficient / the Free-of-Need / the Rich — the One utterly independent and in need of nothing, possessing all wealth; as a human trait it means rich or free from want.
9.grammar: An intensive adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern (denoting a deep, established quality), with 'the'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as a subject or the thing being described.
9.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'He wills, wishes, or so chooses' — to want and intend something by sovereign decision. The root denotes willing and desiring as an act of the will.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'). This is a hollow verb (the weak letter sits in the middle of the root, with hamza as the strong final radical). In the jussive/conditional mood the medial long vowel is shortened (giving 'yashaʾ' rather than 'yashāʾ') — the form taken after 'if' or in a conditional clause.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'He takes you (plural) away,' 'He causes you to depart,' or 'He does away with you' — to remove or make something go. It carries an attached object 'you all.'
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'), in the causative pattern ('to make go / take away'), with the attached object -kum ('you all'). The unvowelled final stem consonant marks the jussive/conditional mood, as in the answer to an 'if.'

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'and He brings, comes with, or produces' — to come bearing something, hence to bring it forth. It joins to what precedes with a connective 'and.'
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'), prefixed with 'and.' The final weak letter is trimmed, marking the jussive/conditional mood — the form taken in the answer to a condition or after 'if.'

5.meaning: A creation; a created thing, a brought-into-being entity, a making. The word denotes both the act of creating and the creature or formation that results.
5.grammar: A singular verbal noun meaning 'creation / a created thing,' preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/of'). The -in ending marks it indefinite ('a creation') and in the genitive case — the case required here by the preceding preposition bi-. The doubled -in (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness.
5.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, fashion, bring into being

6.meaning: New, fresh, recently brought into being; novel. An adjective describing something newly made, as opposed to old or worn.
6.grammar: A singular adjective on the faʿīl pattern, meaning 'new/fresh.' The -in ending marks it indefinite ('a new one / new') and in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun ('… of …'). The doubled -in (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness. The -in here mirrors the case of the noun it describes.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
2.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

3.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
3.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
3.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'Mighty / strong / dear' — one who is powerful and unassailable, hard to overcome and highly esteemed. The faʿīl pattern gives an intensive, enduring sense.
5.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to an intensive adjective. The final -in is the indefinite genitive ending, which a noun takes after a preposition; the genitive is the case that typically follows prepositions or links a word to a preceding one.
5.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, being unassailable and honoured

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: It bears, carries, or takes on (a burden) — especially to carry the weight of sin or responsibility. The verb conveys shouldering a load of guilt or accountability.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular ('she/it …') or second-person masculine singular ('you …') subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, marking ongoing/general action: 'bears / carries'. The verb specifically evokes carrying a load of sin.

3.meaning: A bearer of burden, a burdened soul — one (especially a person) who carries a load, above all the weight of their own sins. As an active participle it names the one doing the bearing.
3.grammar: A Form I feminine active participle, 'a bearer of burden', a single word whose initial wāw is the first radical of the root (not a conjunction). It is feminine because the implied subject 'soul' (nafs) is grammatically feminine. The final -un is the nominative case with nunation ('a …', indefinite), typically marking the subject.

4.meaning: A burden, load, or weight of sin — the heavy charge of guilt and accountability that a person carries for their wrongdoing.
4.grammar: A noun 'wizr' on the pattern 'fiʿl'. The final -a is the accusative case, typically marking the direct object of a verb ('carries a burden') or the thing acted upon. The word denotes a load, especially the weight of sin.

6.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
6.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

7.meaning: You call upon, invoke, pray to, or summon. The verb daʿā covers calling out to someone, appealing to them for help, and supplication.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person-masculine-singular subject ('you'). Built on a root whose last letter is weak: in the plain indicative this verb ends in a long -ū (tadʿū), but here the weak letter has dropped away, leaving the bare short -u of the shortened (jussive) form — the shape this verb takes after certain particles or in conditional clauses.
7.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
9.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
13.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
13.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

14.meaning: A thing, something, anything — an indefinite term for any item, matter, or entity, however small. In negations it yields the sense 'nothing at all'.
14.grammar: The final -un (an 'n'-sound called nunation) marks the noun as indefinite — 'a thing / some thing' rather than 'the thing' — and the -u within it is the nominative case, typically the subject form.

15.meaning: 'And even if / and though' — a particle pairing 'and' with 'law', which introduces a hypothetical or concessive condition ('even supposing that …').
15.grammar: A compound particle: 'and' + the conditional 'law'. 'Law' introduces a supposition, often a counter-to-expectation one ('even if …'), and is typically followed by a past-tense verb that carries a hypothetical sense. It is a function word with no case ending.

16.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

16.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

17.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'this one' or 'the one' — a pointing word ('that/this') used to single out a person or thing. It often combines with the question particle to form 'who is it that…?'
17.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this/that one'). It does not take case endings; the final -ā is part of the fixed word. It functions to point out or identify someone or something.

18.meaning: Kinship / nearness of relation — closeness in family ties; a near relative or the bond of being related. Built from the sense of 'nearness.'
18.grammar: A feminine singular noun ending in alif maqṣūra (-ā). This fixed -ā ending does not change for case, so it can serve in any grammatical position; the word denotes kinship or close relationship.

19.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
19.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

20.meaning: You warn / you can warn: to put someone on guard about a danger or coming consequence so that he may heed it, addressed to a single male 'you'. It denotes the ongoing act of delivering a warning.
20.grammar: A present/imperfect Form IV verb. The prefix tu- marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'); the final -u is the indicative ending, the plain form used for ongoing or habitual action ('you warn / do warn'). Form IV gives the causative 'to make wary, to warn'.
20.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, to caution of consequences

21.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
21.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

22.meaning: 'They fear' or 'they hold in awe' — experiencing khashya, a fear mixed with reverence and awareness of someone's greatness, especially the kind of dread that comes from knowledge of the one feared.
22.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The -awna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject (the long final root-vowel blends into the plural ending) and the indicative mood, which states the action as an ongoing or habitual fact.
22.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — fear blended with awe and reverence

23.meaning: Their Lord, Master, and Sustainer — 'rabb' is the one who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached pronoun, the Lord who is theirs.
23.grammar: A masculine noun with the possessive 'their' attached. The -a vowel before -hum marks the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb.

24.meaning: 'In the unseen' — the preposition 'in/by' with 'the unseen': that which is hidden from perception, beyond what the senses can reach (such as Allah, the angels, and the Hereafter). It denotes the realm one cannot directly observe yet may affirm.
24.grammar: A preposition bi- joined to a definite masculine singular noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition — hence 'in the unseen'. The article al- makes it 'the unseen' as a known whole rather than 'an unseen thing'.
24.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — being hidden, absent from sight

25.meaning: And they established / set up and kept up — they put a thing firmly in place and maintained it duly. Often used of upholding prayer, i.e. performing it properly and consistently.
25.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb on a causative pattern (Form IV, 'to make stand, to set up and keep up'); the -ū ending is the subject 'they' (masculine plural), marking a completed action they performed.
25.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; (causative) to set up, uphold

26.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
26.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

27.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
27.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

29.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
29.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

31.meaning: For / to himself / for his own soul — nafs means the self, soul, or person (the inner self that is held to account). The li- means 'for/to,' and the attached -hi makes it 'his.'
31.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('for/to') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). After the preposition the noun is in the genitive, shown by the -i vowel before the -hi suffix.
31.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person, the inner being

32.meaning: And to / and toward; a connector "and" joined with a preposition expressing direction or destination toward which something moves or is referred.
32.grammar: A preposition meaning "to/toward," prefixed with the connector wa- ("and"). Being a preposition, it puts the noun that follows it into the genitive case (the "…toward X" relationship). It has no case ending of its own.

33.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
33.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

34.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
34.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
34.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'They are equal / it is the same' — to be on a par, level, or alike; to stand even with one another with no difference of value.
2.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is equal'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a present action; the weak final letter (from the root's last 'w/y') appears as the long ending. It expresses things being on the same level.

3.meaning: 'The blind one' — a person lacking sight. Often used figuratively for one who cannot perceive truth or guidance.
3.grammar: A definite descriptive noun/adjective ('the blind') marked by 'al-' ('the'), built on the pattern used for colours and bodily traits. It ends in a fixed long '-ā' vowel and does not change its ending for case — the form stays the same whether subject or object.
3.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — blindness, loss of sight or insight

4.meaning: 'And the seeing one' — a person who possesses sight; figuratively one who perceives clearly and has insight. Built on the intensive 'doer' pattern, it suggests one fully endowed with vision.
4.grammar: A definite noun/adjective joined by 'wa' ('and') and marked by 'al-' ('the'). It follows the 'faʿīl' pattern, which describes someone strongly characterized by a quality (here, seeing). The '-u' ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'the darknesses / the depths of darkness' (plural of 'darkness'). It denotes layers or kinds of darkness, and is often used figuratively for misguidance, ignorance, and disbelief as opposed to light.
2.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun (with al-, 'the'). The -āt is the sound feminine plural ending ('multiple darknesses'). The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is a subject or the thing being described.

3.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
3.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
6.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
7.root: — (proper name)

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

10.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
10.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
12.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

14.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
14.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
2.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

4.meaning: A warner — one who gives warning, alerting people to impending danger or consequence so they may take heed. It names the agent who delivers such an admonition.
4.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive agent-pattern (faʿīl), denoting one who does something fully or by office — a 'warner'. The ending -un is nominative and indefinite ('a warner'); the nominative marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate, so this typically stands as 'is a warner' or 'a warner (came)'.
4.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice of danger

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: 'We sent you / We dispatched you' — the act of sending forth one male addressee, as one is sent on a mission or as a messenger.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV ('afʿala') pattern (to send), with two attached pronouns: 'nā' is the subject 'we,' and the final 'ka' is the object 'you' (one male). So it states a completed act, 'we sent you.'

3.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
3.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

4.meaning: One who carries glad tidings; a herald or announcer of good news, a bringer of joy and welcome promises.
4.grammar: An intensive/agent noun on the pattern faʿīl, naming someone characterized by giving good news. The final -an (accusative with nunation, the doubled 'n' sound) marks it as indefinite and typically signals an object of a verb or a state/role ('as a …'). The nunation shows it is indefinite ('a bringer of good news').
4.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; (also) human skin/mankind

5.meaning: One who warns; a herald who cautions of impending danger or consequence, urging heedfulness.
5.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The stem is an intensive/agent noun on the faʿīl pattern, naming one who warns. The final -an (accusative with nunation) marks it indefinite and typically signals an object or a state/role ('as a …').
5.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution; a solemn vow/pledge

6.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
6.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
8.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'to be/become empty, vacant, or free of others'; idiomatically 'to be alone with someone' or 'to withdraw in private (with another)'. The basic image is a space cleared of all but those concerned.

parts.en: he was alone / withdrew in private

10.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it was empty' or 'he withdrew privately'. The final long -ā reflects a weak (final-vowel) root and marks the bare 'he did' form, with no added subject suffix.
10.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — being empty, vacant, alone, or free of others

11.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
11.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

12.meaning: A warner — one who gives warning, alerting people to impending danger or consequence so they may take heed. It names the agent who delivers such an admonition.
12.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive agent-pattern (faʿīl), denoting one who does something fully or by office — a 'warner'. The ending -un is nominative and indefinite ('a warner'); the nominative marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate, so this typically stands as 'is a warner' or 'a warner (came)'.
12.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice of danger

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

3.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
3.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'he denied / cried lies against / rejected as false' — to treat something or someone as a lie, refusing to accept it as true and openly rejecting it.
4.grammar: Past-tense verb (form II, intensive), third-person masculine singular ('he denied / rejected as false'). The doubled middle letter (kadhdhaba) gives the sense of actively declaring something false. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a masculine singular doer.
4.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (form II) to deny, to call a lie

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
7.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
7.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'she/it came to them' — the act of coming or arriving, directed toward a group of people. Built on the verb 'to come,' with the comers' goal ('them') attached.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb 'came.' The -t suffix is the feminine marker, showing the subject is grammatically feminine ('she/it came') or a feminine plural such as 'messengers/signs.' The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males or mixed).

9.meaning: Their messengers — the envoys or apostles sent by Allah, here belonging to 'them'; 'rusul' is the plural of 'rasūl', one who is dispatched bearing a message.
9.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -hum ending means 'their' (for a group of males). The -u vowel before it is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a sentence.
9.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, an envoy

10.meaning: 'With the clear proofs / evident signs' — bayyināt are plain, self-evident demonstrations that make the truth manifest, leaving no doubt.
10.grammar: Built from 'bi-' ('with/by means of') + 'al-' ('the') + a feminine plural noun meaning 'clear proofs.' The -i ending is the genitive case, required after the preposition 'bi-'; the feminine sound plural '-āt' takes -i (not -a) in this case. The whole phrase means 'with the clear proofs.'

13.meaning: The giving-light / illuminating — that which sheds light, radiant and clarifying; descriptive of something that makes things visible or evident.
13.grammar: An active participle (form IV) meaning 'one that gives light', with the definite article 'al-' (the). The final '-i' (kasra) is the definite genitive: it typically follows a preposition or oath particle, or agrees in case with a preceding noun it describes.
13.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — light, to illuminate

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: So how? / Then in what manner or state? — kayfa is the interrogative 'how', asking after the manner, condition or circumstance of something. With the prefixed 'so/then' it introduces a question following from what precedes, often expressing wonder or warning.
5.grammar: An interrogative particle ('how') carrying the connective prefix fa- ('so / then'), which links it to a preceding statement as a consequence or follow-up. As a particle, kayfa is indeclinable: its fixed final -a is not a case ending and does not change.

6.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

6.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
3.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
5.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
7.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
7.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

8.meaning: 'water' — water in general, the fluid essential to life; also used for liquid such as rain. A basic noun for the substance of water.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case together with indefiniteness — commonly the role of a direct object, the thing acted upon (e.g. what is sent down or brought).

9.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'so We brought out / then We brought forth' — to cause something to emerge or come out from a source.
9.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb in the causative (form IV) pattern, which carries the sense of 'making something come out.' The attached -nā ending marks the doer as 'we.' The prefixed fa- is a connective particle meaning 'so' or 'then,' linking what follows to what came before.

10.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

14.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
14.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

15.meaning: 'The mountains' — the plural of 'mountain', denoting great masses of rock rising from the earth; firm, towering heights.
15.grammar: A definite plural noun: al- is 'the', and the -i (genitive) ending is the case taken after a preposition or when the noun is linked to / possessed by another. It is the broken (irregular) plural of the word for 'mountain'.
15.root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l) — mountain; that which is firmly fixed, innate constitution

19.meaning: An active participle meaning "differing, varied, of varying kinds" — describing something that is diverse, mixed, or not uniform.
19.grammar: An active participle of Form VIII, masculine singular. The -un ending is nominative and indefinite ("a varied [thing]"), the case typically used for a subject or predicate. It denotes an ongoing quality: "being varied/different."
19.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to differ, come after, succeed; difference, variation

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
1.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

2.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
2.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
2.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

4.meaning: 'and livestock / grazing cattle' — the collective term for domesticated grazing animals such as camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; a form of wealth and sustenance.
4.grammar: A connecting wa- ('and') + the article al- ('the') + anʿām, the plural of naʿam ('grazing livestock'). The final -i marks the genitive case, typically signalling that the word is linked to a preceding noun or follows a preposition. The root conveys 'soft living, bounty,' fitting animals that are a source of ease and provision.
4.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — bounty, ease, comfort / grazing livestock

6.meaning: 'Its colors / its hues' — the various shades and tints belonging to a single thing, with the attached pronoun pointing back to the masculine thing that possesses them.
6.grammar: A plural noun (of lawn, 'color') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending (nominative) typically marks it as a subject; the attached -hu means 'its/his', referring to a single masculine owner.

7.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
7.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
7.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

8.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
8.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
14.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
15.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

16.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
16.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").

17.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
17.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They recite / they read out; they read aloud and follow word for word — especially the reciting of a revealed scripture, conveying both 'to read' and 'to follow.'
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they recite,' from a defective root whose final letter is a weak wāw. The ya- prefix with the -ūna suffix marks a third-person masculine plural ('they'). Because the root ends in a weak wāw, that wāw contracts with the plural suffix to produce a single long -ū sound (so the stem's last consonant is not separately heard); the -na of -ūna is the indicative marker for an actual, ongoing, or habitual action.
3.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

4.meaning: A word meaning 'a decree' or 'a prescription' — literally 'a writing.' It denotes something written down and so binding, an ordinance or prescribed duty.
4.grammar: A noun on the pattern fiʿāl carrying the accusative case-vowel -a. The accusative is the ending used for the object of a verb and also for an emphatic verbal noun placed as a kind of stamp on a statement (e.g., '… as an ordained prescription'). Without the article and without tanwīn here, it stands in a possessive ('… of') link with a following word.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: And they established / set up and kept up — they put a thing firmly in place and maintained it duly. Often used of upholding prayer, i.e. performing it properly and consistently.
6.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb on a causative pattern (Form IV, 'to make stand, to set up and keep up'); the -ū ending is the subject 'they' (masculine plural), marking a completed action they performed.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; (causative) to set up, uphold

7.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
7.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.
7.root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — prayer, worship, supplication

8.meaning: And they spent or laid out — to disburse wealth, expending it (especially in giving and charitable outlay).
8.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV) prefixed with 'wa' (and). The suffix '-ū' is the subject ending for a third-person masculine plural — 'they (did it)' — marking a completed action carried out by a group.

9.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
9.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.
